instructions.title: Instructions for Claude
instructions.lede: What Claude is told about this world before it writes for it through the MCP server: the setting first, then what each kind of thing should be like. Only Claude reads these.
instructions.setting_hint: Which world this is and when: its lands, cities, peoples, factions, gods, tone — and how its races and creatures map onto 5e.
instructions.setting_example: This world is the Sunken Marches, river country where the old dam broke. Use its towns, ferries and people (Grey Reed, the toll bridge at Lowmere, the drowned chapel …). Races: the river folk are halflings, the Reedfolk lizardfolk. Monsters unknown to 5e are reskins of book creatures: Mire Lurkers are Kuo-toa, toll robbers are Bandits.
instructions.adventure_hint: Length, tone, structure, what to avoid.
instructions.adventure_example: Two sessions; one clear villain; a choice that changes the ending; no world-ending stakes.
instructions.chapter_hint: How chapters are written and laid out.
instructions.chapter_example: Each chapter opens with a read-aloud box; secrets in a secret box; at most one fight per chapter.
instructions.npc_hint: Names, factions, how they speak; known figures of the setting and the statblocks they use.
instructions.npc_example: Every NPC belongs to a town or a band (Grey Reed, the Rotfang goblins, the ferry guild). Known figures keep their story: Old Gnasher is a Bugbear, Hob Wade a Commoner.

corpus.kind.unreadable: Files that are not valid JSON
corpus.hint.unreadable: The file was skipped entirely. Usually a truncated download or a hand edit.
corpus.kind.not_object: Files that are not a JSON object
corpus.hint.not_object: 5eTools files hold an object of arrays; this one holds something else and was skipped.
corpus.hint.bad_row: An array of entries holds something that is not an entry; it was skipped.
corpus.hint.invalid: The entry lacks a field Paravent needs or holds one in a shape it cannot read. It is missing from search and from every link to it.
corpus.kind.unresolved_copy: Copies of entries that do not exist
corpus.hint.unresolved_copy: The entry is a patch (_copy) of another entry that was not found, so it was skipped.
corpus.kind.unknown_copy_mode: Patch modes Paravent does not know
corpus.hint.unknown_copy_mode: A _copy patch uses a mode added upstream. The patch was skipped, so the entries using it are subtly wrong.
corpus.hint.missing_template: A creature names a template (bestiary/template.json) that does not exist; it loads without it.
corpus.hint.missing_item_entry: An item's text is a {#itemEntry} reference to shared text in items-base.json that does not exist; the item shows the reference.
corpus.hint.unfilled_item_entry: Shared item text asks the item for a value (a colour, a damage type) it does not have; the gap shows as written.
corpus.kind.count_mismatch: Counts that do not add up
corpus.hint.count_mismatch: The store holds a different number of entries than the files explain — entries were lost or invented somewhere without a report.
corpus.hint.fluff_invalid: A fluff record (description, images) could not be read; its entry shows without it.
corpus.kind.fluff_unresolved: Descriptions copying one that does not exist
corpus.hint.fluff_unresolved: A fluff record copies another that was not found.
corpus.hint.table_unreadable: A table a feature reads (treasure, encounters, names, creature builder) has changed shape upstream.
corpus.hint.unknown_key: New upstream, most likely: nothing reads it, and nothing was planned for it.
corpus.hint.missing_file: The feature that reads this file has nothing to show.
corpus.hint.table_empty: The file was read, but the feature found none of the tables it looks for.
corpus.kind.missing_body: Books and adventures without their text
corpus.hint.missing_body: The index lists it, but its text file is missing; it shows in lists and cannot be opened.
corpus.hint.unindexed_body: A book or adventure text that books.json or adventures.json does not mention cannot be reached.
corpus.kind.lookup_missing: Spell lists naming spells not loaded
corpus.hint.lookup_missing: The spell-list lookup names spells of a book whose spells are not loaded.
corpus.hint.unknown_tag: A tag new upstream: it shows as its plain text until the renderer learns it.
corpus.hint.duplicate_key: Two rows share a name and book; the later one is kept.
corpus.hint.fluff_orphans: Normal in part: some describe creature groups or are only copied from.
corpus.hint.dead_reference: Tags naming an entry no loaded book holds (often a table inside a rulebook or an item group). They show as grey text.
corpus.hint.translation_stale: The English changed since these passages were translated. They still show, marked as outdated; the link opens them beside the new English.

corpus.hint.translation_lost: The entry, chapter or book these translate is no longer in the data, or goes by another name. They stay in the file; nothing shows them.
corpus.hint.translation_tags: Tags of the English that the translation lacks: a link or a roll the reader does not get.
corpus.hint.translation_link: Tags in translated text naming an entry no loaded book holds. They show as grey text.
corpus.kind.glossary_lost: Names of entries that are gone
corpus.hint.glossary_lost: Glossary names whose English entry is no longer in the data, or goes by another name. Harmless, but the name no longer shows.

seeds.villain.no_tables: The world's books have no villain tables: they are in the 2014 Dungeon Master's Guide.
seeds.adventure.title: Ideas for {name}
seeds.adventure.lede: A situation or goal, a hook, the people involved, a twist and a climax, from the guides' tables. Tick what to keep; it goes at the end of the adventure's text, in a secret box.
seeds.adventure.no_tables: The world's books have no adventure tables: they are in the Dungeon Master's Guides.
seeds.adventure.level: The situation fits a party of level {level}.
gift.read_hint: Read from its text; change them if the table decides otherwise. Empty: no limit.
gift.heading: Supernatural gifts
gift.use_hint: Spend one use; the last makes it vanish.
gift.end_hint: The character no longer holds it.
gift.error.unknown: This gift is not in the world's books.
protocol.formula_taken: no longer holds the formula for {name}
crafting.heading: Magic item formulas
crafting.lede.xdmg: Crafting by the 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide: proficiency in Arcana, the item's tool and its spells prepared; the cost is paid when the work starts.
crafting.lede.xge: Crafting by Xanathar's Guide: the appropriate tool or Arcana, and an exotic material the gamemaster sends you after; the cost is paid when the work starts.
crafting.lede.dmg: Crafting by the 2014 Dungeon Master's Guide: a spellcaster with spell slots who can cast the item's spells, from a level by its rarity; 25 gp of work each day.
crafting.no_rule: The world's books have no rules for crafting magic items.
crafting.no_row: The guide prices no item of this rarity.
crafting.ingredient: an exotic material: a challenge of CR {cr}
crafting.missing.arcana_or_tool: Needs proficiency in Arcana or the appropriate tool.
crafting.give_hint: Who holds the formula may craft this item in downtime.
crafting.error.unknown: This magic item is not in the world's books.
menu.speaker: Play on the speaker
hand.give_lede: It goes into the other character's pack, with its charges and whatever the gamemaster knows of it. The log says who gave what to whom.
hand.drop_lede: It leaves the pack and the sheet. This cannot be undone; the log keeps a line of it.
hand.worn_hint: Worn or attuned now: it comes off first.
travel.helped_hint: An accurate map, or the sun or stars in view: advantage on navigating
travel.helped_hint_one: Another character helps the navigator: advantage on navigating
travel.stealthy_hint: Only at a slow pace, and not in the open
travel.stealthy_hint_one: With disadvantage on Stealth at a normal or fast pace

travel.lost.one: {name} lost the way on 1 day, {distance} astray
travel.lost.other: {name} lost the way on {n} days, {distance} astray

travel.foraged: Foraged {food} of food and {water} of water; {meals} meals instead of rations
travel.ambush: If they lie in wait (Stealth {stealth}), surprised: {names}
worlds.combat_rules_hint: From the 2014 Dungeon Master's Guide; the tracker applies them. A fight keeps the rules it started with.
worlds.rule.massive_damage_hint: Half the maximum HP or more from one source calls a DC 15 Constitution save; a failure rolls on the guide's System Shock table.
worlds.rule.injuries_hint: A character who takes a critical hit or drops to 0 HP may roll on the guide's table; the injury stays on the sheet until you end it.
worlds.rule.morale_hint: A group that has lost half its number, or a lone creature at half its HP, is reminded once to make a DC 10 Wisdom save or flee.
worlds.rule.mobs_hint: Many creatures of one group attacking one target roll no attacks: the guide's table says how many hit.
worlds.rule.side_initiative_hint: Each side rolls one d20; the whole of the higher side acts first.
combat.rule.sides: Side initiative: the party {friend}, their foes {foe}
combat.rule.massive_made: {subject}: massive damage — Constitution save {amount} against DC {dc}, made
combat.rule.massive_failed: {subject}: massive damage — Constitution save {amount} against DC {dc}, failed
combat.rule.morale_made: {subject}: morale — Wisdom save {amount} against DC {dc}, they stand
combat.rule.morale_failed: {subject}: morale — Wisdom save {amount} against DC {dc}, they break and may flee
combat.rule.mob: {subject} ×{n} gang up on {target} with {action}: {per} for each hit, {hits} hits, {damage} damage
combat.rule.mob_none: {subject} ×{n} gang up on {target} with {action}: they cannot hit
combat.due_morale_half: {name}: half the group is down — morale, a DC {dc} Wisdom save or flee.
combat.due_morale_hurt: {name}: at half its hit points — morale, a DC {dc} Wisdom save or flee.
combat.injury_due_crit: {name} took a critical hit: a lingering injury?
combat.injury_due_down: {name} dropped to 0 hit points: a lingering injury?
combat.mob_hint: No attack rolls: the guide's Mob Attacks table says how many hit, each hit's damage applied.
combat.error.morale_done: This group's morale was already tested.
combat.error.no_injury: No lingering injury is offered for this character.
combat.error.no_table: The world's books lack the table this rule rolls on.
combat.error.no_ac: The target has no armor class.
worlds.character_rules_hint: From the guides; the sheet and the clock apply them.
worlds.rest_variant_hint: How long a rest takes; what it restores stays the same. A party rest moves the world's clock on by it.
worlds.rest.standard: As in the handbook: short 1 hour, long 8 hours
worlds.rule.rest_epic: Epic heroism: short 5 minutes, long 1 hour
worlds.rule.rest_gritty: Gritty realism: short 8 hours, long 7 days
worlds.rule.hero_points_hint: 5 at 1st level, then 5 + half the level at each new level. One adds a d6 to an attack roll, a check or a save just rolled, or turns a failed death save into a success.
worlds.rule.honor_hint: A seventh ability score with checks and saves; the gamemaster raises or lowers it by 1 at the end of an adventure.
worlds.rule.sanity_hint: An ability score with checks and saves, for campaigns where the mind is at risk.
worlds.rule.slow_healing_hint: A long rest restores no hit points; hit dice are spent at its end instead.
worlds.rule.healers_kit_hint: After a rest, no hit dice are spent until a use of a healer's kit has treated the wounds.
worlds.rule.defeated_hint: From the 2024 guide: a character who would die lies unconscious at 1 hit point until a Greater Restoration, or a DC 20 Constitution save after a long rest.
sheet.score_ask: This world plays with these scores. Set yours once; afterwards the gamemaster changes it.
sheet.hero_point_hint: Spend one on your last roll: a d6 added to an attack, a check or a save, or a failed death save made a success.
sheet.defeated: Defeated: unconscious until a Greater Restoration, or a DC {dc} Constitution save after each long rest.
sheet.wake_hint: The spell has been cast on the character: it wakes.
sheet.bandaged_hint: A healer's kit treated the wounds; hit dice may be spent until the next rest.
sheet.no_kit: Hit dice need a healer's kit
sheet.bandage_hint: Spend a use of the healer's kit, so hit dice may be spent after this rest.
rule.hero_death: {subject} spends a hero point: the failed death save is a success
rule.defeated: {subject} is defeated, not dead: unconscious at 1 hit point
rule.bandage: {subject}'s wounds are treated with a healer's kit ({left} uses left)
play.error.not_bandaged: Treat the wounds with a healer's kit first.
play.error.no_hero_roll: A hero point goes on the last roll: an attack, a check, a save or a failed death save, one per roll.
play.error.no_healers_kit: No healer's kit in the pack.
play.error.gamemaster_only: Only the gamemaster may change that.
combat.objects_hint: An object or a door: it takes no turn, earns no XP and takes no poison or psychic damage.
combat.object_dc: The DC to force it open
shop.choose: {n} items: choose a shelf or search to see them.
combat.siege_hint: Siege equipment fights for a side: its crew load, aim and fire it on their turns, from its panel's attacks.
copy.lede: Everything is copied with new ids; fights, the log, a quest's characters and renown stay behind.
copy.no_worlds: There is no other world yet. Make one from the world menu first.
copy.bring_hint: The world's own NPCs, places, treasure and encounters its texts link to, and a quest's faction. One the other world already has by that name is not copied: the link finds that one.
copy.brought: Comes along, as its texts name it
copy.not_brought: Named in its texts, left behind
copy.reused: {world} has these already; the links find them there
copy.outside_hint: They are copied as written and show as “not in your books” there, until the world declares the book or you change them.
copy.copy_hint: The original stays as it is.
copy.move_hint: The original goes to Recently deleted, from where it can be restored for 30 days. A quest, faction or creature design has no trash and moves as it is.

copy.outside_done.one: One reference is not in the books of {world}.
copy.outside_done.other: {n} references are not in the books of {world}.

copy.error.no_piece: That is not there any more.
copy.error.same_world: It is in that world already.
copy.renamed_one: “{old}” has a namesake there: the copy is called “{name}”.
copy.file_hint: A file to take to another table: there, Import into this world in the world menu reads it into the world it plays in.
copy.skipped: Left out, as the file did not hold them right: {names}
copy.import_lede: A file saved with “Save as a file” at this or another table: its adventures, NPCs, places, treasure, encounters, quests, factions or creatures join this world with new ids.
copy.import_bring_hint: The NPCs, places, treasure, encounters and factions the file carries because its texts name them. One this world has by that name already is not added: the links find this world's.
copy.error.none: Tick at least one in the list first.
copy.error.mixed: The pieces chosen belong to different worlds; choose from one world at a time.
copy.error.not_pieces: That is not a file saved with “Save as a file”.
copy.error.newer: The file comes from a newer Paravent; update this one first.
